sections.title: Purpose and Anchored System Service Life
sections.summary: GEC-4 provides state-of-the-practice information on cement-grouted, prestressed ground anchors and anchored systems for highway applications. Covered systems include flexible anchored walls, slope and landslide stabilization, and tiedown anchors. Permanent anchored systems have a service life of 75–100 years. Temporary systems are defined as those removed or inoperative within 18–36 months. Critical temporary systems are designed to the same criteria as permanent systems. SOE (support of excavation) temporary systems are designed to less restrictive criteria.
sections.body:
The purpose of this document is to provide state-of-the-practice information on ground anchors and anchored systems for highway applications. Ground anchors discussed are cement-grouted, prestressed tendons installed in soil or rock. Anchored systems include flexible anchored walls, slopes supported using ground anchors, slope and landslide stabilization systems, and tiedown anchors. Design, construction, and load testing methods described are those currently used in U.S. practice.

Permanent anchored systems are generally considered to have a service life of 75 to 100 years. Temporary systems have a service life of 18 to 36 months (or shorter/longer based on project conditions). This document subdivides temporary systems into 'support of excavation' (SOE) and 'critical' temporary systems. Critical temporary systems are designed to the same criteria as permanent systems. SOE systems are designed to less restrictive criteria (the contractor typically owns design responsibility). Design components that are less restrictive for SOE vs. permanent systems: (1) selection of timber lagging; (2) allowable stresses; (3) factors of safety; (4) axial load design; (5) surcharge loads; (6) seismic design criteria; and (7) anchor load testing.
key_points: Covers cement-grouted prestressed anchors in soil/rock; anchored walls, slope stabilization, tiedown anchors
Temporary systems: 18–36 months; critical temporary systems designed to same criteria as permanent
SOE systems: less restrictive on lagging, allowable stress, FS, axial load, surcharge, seismic, and load testing

sections.title: Background
sections.summary: GEC-4 updates the FHWA (1988) design manual 'Permanent Ground Anchors' (FHWA-DP-68-1R). Key reference documents incorporated: AASHTO Task Force 27 (1990) 'In-Situ Soil Improvement Techniques' (generic ground anchor spec and inspection manual); PTI (1996) 'Recommendations for Prestressed Rock and Soil Anchors'. FHWA research from the 1990s on full-scale anchored walls (FHWA-RD-98-066, -067, -97-130) provides the basis for several design procedures adopted herein.
sections.body:
Ground anchors were first used in the U.S. for temporary SOE systems by specialty contractors. Permanent ground anchor use for public highway projects became common only in the late 1970s. In 1979, FHWA authorized a permanent ground anchor demonstration project; two FHWA research reports (FHWA-RD-81-150/151/152) and a design manual (1984, updated 1988 as FHWA-DP-68-1R) were produced. During the demonstration project, five U.S. highway projects with permanent anchored systems were instrumented (FHWA-DP-90-068-003, 1990).

GEC-4 was written to update the 1988 manual. Since 1988, advances include performance data from anchored wall monitoring, new construction materials and methods, and improved acceptance testing procedures. Most recently, FHWA research (FHWA-RD-97-130, -98-066, -98-067, 1998) on full-scale and large-scale model anchored walls provides the basis for several design procedures adopted herein. AASHTO Task Force 27 (1990) and PTI (1996) form the basis for the chapters on load testing and corrosion protection and for the generic ground anchor specification in Appendix E.
key_points: AASHTO Task Force 27 (1990) and PTI (1996) form the basis for load testing and corrosion chapters
FHWA-RD-97-130/98-066/98-067 research on full-scale and model walls informs design procedures
Generic ground anchor specification provided in Appendix E; Appendix F is anchored wall specification
